Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Chilliwack Mountain

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The 2050 Official Community Plan’s Schedule D lists D-2 Hillside Environment and D-5 Hillside Development as development permit areas.
The City’s DPA-2 (Hillside Environment) guide lists Chilliwack Mountain among its designated hillside and upland areas.

A DPA-2 permit is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. The application needs a geotechnical report by a registered geotechnical engineer, including a hazard and slope assessment, setbacks, cut and fill considerations and site stability.
Development on Chilliwack Mountain is governed by the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan and DPA-2 Hillside rules.
The City’s Schweyey Road forcemain page says the pipe along Schweyey Road provides sewage services for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way.
ALR: Published municipal records list no statement specific to Chilliwack Mountain. City-wide, the City says nearly 70% of the land in Chilliwack is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.

Flood: Published municipal records list no flood note specific to Chilliwack Mountain. The City’s Fraser River Flood Protection page describes the dyke system and says areas outside the City’s dyking system flood at higher river stages.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Chilliwack Mountain

parts.t: Check the hillside rules.
Ask the City whether a DPA-2 permit applies to the lot, and what the geotechnical report would need to cover.
Look at slope and drainage.
Check the ground around the home for slope, drainage and any past movement, and have the inspector look at it.
Confirm the school catchment.
There is no SD33 school on the mountain, so use the SD33 School Locator for the exact address.
Check the ALR on larger lots.
Look up the address on the Agricultural Land Commission map before you plan anything on farmland.
Check how you will get around.
There is no bus route named for the mountain, so plan trips around Route 59’s limited weekday peak trips or a car.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.

FAQ
Where is Chilliwack Mountain?
The City of Chilliwack doesn’t publish a street-by-street boundary for the MLS® sub-area Chilliwack Mountain.
BC Geographical Names places the mountain on the south side of the Fraser River, just west of Chilliwack Creek.
Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Chilliwack Mountain?
No route in BC Transit’s Chilliwack route list is named for Chilliwack Mountain.
Route 59 Industrial runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Cottonwood Mall via the Lickman Park and Ride. BC Transit’s page shows peak-period weekday trips only
See the
BC Transit Chilliwack page
Which schools serve Chilliwack Mountain?
There is no SD33 school on Chilliwack Mountain. The Province’s school directory for Chilliwack lists all SD33 schools with addresses, and none has a Chilliwack Mountain address.
Check which school an address is assigned to with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are on or near Chilliwack Mountain?

Hillkeep Regional Park is a 36-acre Fraser Valley Regional District nature reserve at the top of the mountain, with about 2 km of hiking trails and a viewing platform. It is open 7 am to sunset, with limited parking.
No City recreation centre is on Chilliwack Mountain. The nearest is Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre at 9145 Corbould St.
The nearest library is the Chilliwack Library at 45860 First Avenue.
What hillside rules apply on Chilliwack Mountain?
The City’s DPA-2 (Hillside Environment) guide lists Chilliwack Mountain among its designated hillside and upland areas.
A DPA-2 permit is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks, and the application needs a geotechnical report with a hazard and slope assessment.
Ask me or the City whether it applies to a specific lot.
Is Chilliwack Mountain in a floodplain?
Published municipal records list no flood note specific to Chilliwack Mountain. The mountain stands on the south side of the Fraser River.
The City’s Fraser River Flood Protection page describes the dyke system and says areas outside the City’s dyking system flood at higher river stages.
See the
City flood protection page
